confirmed.title: Skating boot pitched toe-down in every new jump load/pick pose: the standing foot is never aimed, so it follows a shin that leans past the booted ankle range
confirmed.claim: None of the 12 jump poses aims the standing foot, so the resolver (limits.ts resolve(): an unposed bone keeps its rest relation to its parent) pitches the blade with the shin. Measured with resolvePose + the GLB lengths (thigh 0.3776, shin 0.371, foot 0.172, socket 0.885): standing blade toe-down beyond rest = axelLoad 39° (shin_L limb(-45) line 178), loopLoad 36° (shin_R limb(-42) line 43), salchowLoad 34° (line 81), lutzPick 30° (line 240), flipPick 26° (line 119), toeLoopPick 26° (line 140); the foot-bone tip sits below the ice in flipPick/toeLoopPick (-0.028 m) and lutzPick (-0.016 m) while the ankle is 2-4 cm lower than standing, i.e. the heel is in the air and the toe through the ice. Pose-lab screenshots of axelLoad, lutzPick and loopLoad (scratchpad/axelLoad.png etc.) show the skating boot standing on its toe. Aiming the foot flat would not fix it either: LIMITS.foot_* cone 95° (limits.ts:99-100) allows only 21° of dorsiflexion past the 74° rest, so the shin can lean at most ~27° with a flat blade (the sitStand comment in poses-spins.ts:134 admits it pins the sit shin at 24°), whereas a deep take-off knee bend, a landing and a sit spin all carry the shin 35-45° forward of vertical with the whole blade on the ice (boot forward flex plus the raised heel).
confirmed.failure: Play any jump on /jumps/[slug] with the side or follow camera: at 'Knee bend' and at the pick the take-off blade tilts 26-39° onto the toe pick with the heel ~10 cm up; the Axel (an edge jump that must leave from a flat forward outside edge) visibly takes off from its toe. The sit spin still shows the knee behind the toe with the hips 0.246 m behind the blade (SIT_HIPS).
confirmed.fix: In limits.ts:99-100 raise the booted ankle cone from 95 to ~110 (dorsiflexion ~35° past rest; keep minAngle 45) and in the jump poses aim the standing foot at its rest direction, as sitStand does: add `foot_L: { dir: vec(0, -0.38, 0.925) }` to salchowLoad, flipPick, axelLoad, lutzPick and `foot_R` to loopLoad/toeLoopPick (and land/landDeep in poses.ts), so the clamp keeps the blade flat; then set sitStand shin_L to limb(-38, 3) and recompute SIT_HIPS.z (~-0.17).

votes.reasoning: The finding is correct and reproducible. In three/rig/limits.ts resolve(), an unposed bone copies its parent's rotation (`q = parent.q.clone()`), so a foot the pose does not aim keeps the 73.7° rest angle to the shin and pitches with it. None of the 12 poses in three/rig/poses-jumps.ts aims the standing foot (loopGlide/loopLoad/loopLaunch/toeLoopPick leave foot_R out; salchowLoad/salchowSwing/flipPick/axelGlide/axelLoad/axelLaunch/lutzGlide/lutzPick leave foot_L out), while every free foot is `pointed()`. Resolving the poses with resolvePose + the GLB lengths quoted in poses-spins.ts (socket 0.885, thigh 0.3776, shin 0.371, foot 0.172, standing ankle 0.139) gives exactly the reviewer's numbers: standing foot pitched beyond rest by +38.9° (axelLoad, shin limb(-45) at line 178), +35.9° (loopLoad), +33.9° (salchowLoad), +29.9° (lutzPick), +25.9° (flipPick, toeLoopPick); foot-bone tip below the ice at -0.028 m (flipPick, toeLoopPick), -0.016 (lutzPick), -0.009 (salchowLoad), and the ankle 3 cm higher than standing in axelLoad (0.170) and loopLoad (0.147), i.e. the hips offsets were tuned with the skater standing on her toe. The pose-lab screenshots (scratchpad/axelLoad.png, lutzPick.png, loopLoad.png) and the orchestrator's own player shots at the "Knee bend" marker (scratchpad/jumps/after-axel-side.png, after-salchow-side.png) show the standing boot with its heel in the air and the toe in the ice. The booted cone in LIMITS (95°, i.e. 21° of dorsiflexion past the 74° rest) is also confirmed as the blocker for the obvious fix: aiming the foot at its rest direction under the current clamp still leaves axelLoad +18.6° and loopLoad +15.6° toe-down (clamped at 94°); with cone 110 the residuals drop to +3.6°/+0.6°/0°. The 95° figure is the non-weight-bearing AAOS goniometric norm; a loaded knee bend with the heel down (weight-bearing lunge test norms of 35-45° shin-to-vertical) plus the boot's raised heel makes ~35° past the booted rest defensible for an elite skater, and the sitStand comment in poses-spins.ts shows the team already had to fight this limit (shin pinned at 24°, hips 0.246 m behind the blade). This is not a documented judgement call for the jump poses: the file header only says free feet are pointed to stay in range, nothing says the standing boot is meant to follow the shin. The same defect pre-exists in loadBO/loadFO/land/landDeep (poses.ts, +23.9° to +38.9°), which the landings still use, so the fix should cover them too. One gap in the proposed fix: flattening the foot without re-tuning the hips leaves the blade 2-4 cm under the ice for the picks (flipPick/toeLoopPick ankle 0.101, lutzPick 0.120) and 3 cm above it for axelLoad (0.170); the hips y of each pose must be recomputed so the ankle returns to 0.139.

votes.reasoning: The finding is correct and user-visible. limits.ts resolve(): an unposed bone keeps its rest relation to its parent, and the booted-ankle clamp only runs for posed feet, so a standing foot that no pose aims simply rides the shin. All six Wave 2 load/pick poses (three/rig/poses-jumps.ts) leave the standing foot unposed with the shin leaning 32-45° forward, so the resolved blade pitches 26-39° toe-down beyond rest. In the rendered rig this is a boot standing on its toe pick with the heel in the air (axelLoad, loopLoad, salchowLoad, loadFO) or a boot pitched nose-down and sunk through the ice (flipPick/toeLoopPick: foot-bone tip at -0.028 m, lutzPick -0.016 m) — visible in the pose lab side camera and on the real jump timeline at the "Knee bend" instant with the Side camera. The same defect pre-exists in poses.ts (loadBO +34°, loadFO +39°, land +24°, landDeep +39°), so the diff did not introduce the mechanism, but it replicated it into every per-jump entry that now drives the viewer, and the booted-ankle clamp added in the same diff (81f3f37) never sees the standing foot. The LIMITS comment documents 95° as the bare-ankle static dorsiflexion (~21°), but the weight-bearing lunge range (shin 35-45° to vertical with the heel down) plus the boot heel make a ~41° shin lean with a flat blade normal, as the reviewer says; the codebase's only documented judgement call (sitStand pinned at 24°) is a concession to the limit, not a defence of toe-down standing boots. The proposed fix validates: with cone 110 and the standing foot aimed at rest, every affected pose and the glide→load, load→launch, open→land, land→landDeep blend midpoints report no ROM violations; no test pins the 95 value. One refinement is needed: the poses' hips.y were tuned for the pitched foot, so with a flat blade the ankle lands 2-4 cm off the ice unless hips.y is retuned.

confirmed.title: Flying camel lands on the left foot (forward camel); a real flying camel lands on the right foot in a back camel
confirmed.claim: spinFromSpec gives the first position foot "L", edge "inside" for every family (lines 565/567/569 pass "L"), and the FCSp preset (line 342) uses the default L. The flying camel (FCSp, FCCSp, FCCoSp, FCSpToeArabian) takes off from the left forward outside edge and lands on the opposite (right) foot on the back outside edge in a back camel; FCCSp/FCCoSp then change to the left foot. The code's own air pose already implies this: flyCamel sweeps thigh_L to limb(-120) with thigh_R at limb(-70) (right leg coming down), yet the probe shows the skater landing on the left ankle (ankleL 0.18 m vs ankleR 1.12 m at spin start) with the trace foot 'L' and the marker 'left back inside edge'.
confirmed.failure: Build FCSp or FCCoSp in the SpinExplorer: the legs swap during the 0.45 s landing blend (right leg down in the air, then standing on the left), the trace and HUD say 'left back inside', and the FCCoSp change of foot goes left to right instead of right to left.
confirmed.fix: In spinFromSpec, when `flying && landing === "camel"` (and in the FCSp/FCSpToeArabian presets) start the first position on foot "R" (edge "outside", mirrored pose) and run the change of foot to "L"/"inside"; keep the flying sit on "L". Make the entry trace foot 'L' and the post-landing trace 'R' (spinTimeline trace loop takes the phase foot already).

votes.reasoning: The claim checks out against the code and against standard technique, and there is no documented judgement call covering it. Technique: for a counter-clockwise skater the flying camel takes off from the left forward outside edge and lands on the opposite (right) foot on the back outside edge in a back camel (the ISU handbook does not fix the foot, but every teaching reference and the code's own description of the Toe Arabian as "a change of foot by jump" imply the foot changes); the flying sit lands on the take-off (left) foot, which the code already does. Code: spinFromSpec passes "L" for the first position of every family (three/animation/spins.ts ~565-571), positionPhases derives edge "inside" from that, and the FCSp / FCSpToeArabian presets use the default L, so every flying camel (FCSp, FCCSp, FCCoSp, FCoSp, Toe Arabian) spins on "left back inside" and FCCSp/FCCoSp change left-to-right. The air pose contradicts this: flyCamel has thigh_L at limb(-120) (y=+0.49, swept up behind) and thigh_R at limb(-70) (y=-0.33, coming down), i.e. the right leg is the landing leg, yet the camel pose stands on thigh_L. The 0.45 s landing blend therefore sweeps the left thigh 121° (Toe Arabian: 149°) while the right thigh rises 38° — the leg swap the reviewer describes — whereas a mirrored camel on the right foot would move thigh_L 12° (Toe Arabian 42°). Nothing in docs/HANDOFF.md or the code records this as a deliberate choice (the conventions only say feet are for a CCW skater), and the fix is contained (spec builder, two presets, two test assertions, one explorer summary line). Severity is better described as medium than high: it is a pedagogical/visual inaccuracy, not a crash.

votes.reasoning: The claim is correct on the skating and reproducible in the code. A standard flying camel (counter-clockwise skater) takes off from the left forward outside edge and lands on the opposite foot, the right, on a back outside edge in a back camel; FCCSp/FCCoSp then change to the left foot. The flying sit lands on the take-off foot. The repo's own air poses already encode the right-foot landing: in `flyCamel` the right leg is the lower one (thigh_R limb(-70) vs thigh_L limb(-120)), and in `toeArabian` even more so, yet `spinFromSpec` passes "L" for the first position of every family (three/animation/spins.ts lines 565/567/569, `positionPhases` then sets edge "inside") and the `FCSp`/`FCSpToeArabian` presets (lines 342, 383) use the default L/inside. The result is a reverse scissor in the landing blend: the high left leg drops 90° to become the skating leg while the lower right leg is lifted back up to horizontal. It is user-visible in three places: the HUD marker for the flying camel says "left back inside edge", the explorer's "Revolutions counted" panel says "Camel position · left foot", and the change of foot in FCCSp/FCCoSp runs left-to-right. Nothing documents this as a judgement call: docs/HANDOFF.md, data/spins.ts and the ISU texts in docs/isu/text never prescribe the landing foot; the only places that encode "first foot is L" are tests/spins.test.ts lines 108–109 and 124, which pin the convention rather than the biomechanics. The fix is small (positionPhases already mirrors poses and derives the edge from the foot; `mirrorPose` mirrors the hips offset; the lean sign for R/outside equals L/inside so the trace and lean need no change; the trace loop already takes the phase foot), and it improves the landing motion: flyCamel → mirrored camel moves the right thigh −71°→+3° (the lower leg comes down) and settles the left from −120° to −92°, instead of swapping legs. It does require updating two test assertions and one explorer line, which is a cost, not a reason to keep the error on a site judged on anatomical correctness.

confirmed.title: Camel upward/sideways rotate the lumbar spine ~90° while the pelvis stays flat (no derived pelvis twist, no trunk twist limit)
confirmed.claim: camelUpward sets spine twist 1.6 rad (92°) and chest twist 2.6 rad (149°), camelSideways 0.9/1.4 rad (52°/80°). These twists are absolute (resolve(): q = qAxis(dir, twist)·swing from rest) and the derived pelvis always gets `twist: 0` (limits.ts:450), so the whole shoulder-line rotation is taken by the lumbar (~90° in CU, ~50° in CS) and thoracic segments; anatomically the lumbar rotates ~10-15° and the thoracic ~35-45°, and the remainder in a real CS/CU comes from the pelvis opening about the standing hip (the table itself grants the hip 60° of axial rotation). validatePose never checks any `twist`, so nothing catches it.
